subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state
snippet: Follow-up on tokens/sec, QPS, peak vs steady-state and next steps for SLO review call.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Kerr <sam.kerr@finex.io>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@finex.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what I heard on throughput and SLOs so we can align before the technical deep-dive: 

- Primary use: chat-like assistant embedded in Finex web app (mixed prompt lengths, median ~60 tokens, 95p ~450 tokens).
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms for interactive responses (streaming preferred).
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~8 rps during business hours.
- Peak: up to ~120 concurrent users during batch jobs / market opens — rough peak QPS ~40-50 for short bursts.
- Concurrency/streams: many sessions are long-lived with streaming token-by-token; need to support 40–60 concurrent streaming sessions with low tail latency.
- Throughput requirement: goal is ~1200–1500 tokens/sec aggregate during peak bursts (estimate).

Questions for your engineering team before our SLO call: 
1) Are there hard limits on per-session token budget? (e.g., max sequence length)
2) What fraction of calls will be streaming vs non-streaming?
3) Do you expect many long prefix-shared prompts (so KV-cache reuse helps)?

I've attached a small sizing worksheet that outlines assumptions and a first-cut tokens/sec -> GPU mapping. Rafael and Vivek are CC'd to add any runtime/quantization notes.

Next step: if this summary looks correct, propose a 30-minute SLO/architecture call early next week to validate numbers and run a short perf test.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: throughput_estimate.xlsx (16KB)

From: Samuel Kerr <sam.kerr@finex.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@finex.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sequence lengths: yes, median ~60 tokens, tail up to ~600 tokens for some analyst workflows, but those are ~5% of calls.
- Streaming: roughly 70% of user-facing calls will be streaming token-by-token; the rest are batch requests (non-streaming) for higher-quality outputs.
- Per-session budget: we cap at 2,048 tokens, but most sessions stay under 1,000.
- Peak behavior: the 40–50 QPS bursts are accurate, but those bursts can be very short (30–90s) and happen multiple times a day around market open/close.

We attached the call recording for context.

Sam
Samuel Kerr
Lead Product Manager, Finex
sam.kerr@finex.io
Attachment: finex_call_recording.mp4 (4.2MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Kerr <sam.kerr@finex.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 17:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state

Perfect — that's helpful. Based on that, a few notes and an ask: 

Notes:
- We'll size for the burst case but optimize for cost in steady-state via batching and KV caching. If tail calls are 5% but 95p up to 600 tokens, that changes peak token load significantly.
- Streaming sessions are more sensitive to p95 tail; we'll look at instance types that reduce tail latency and support streaming prefetching.

Ask: could you share a short sample of request length distribution (CSV or histogram) and an example of a heavily prefixed prompt (so Rafael can estimate KV-cache hit rate)? If you want, we can do a 90-minute perf session where Finex sends a recorded workload to a test endpoint and we run a short load test.

I've updated the sizing sheet with two scenarios (conservative peak and optimized steady-state). See attachment.

Thanks —
Marissa
Attachment: throughput_estimate.xlsx (updated)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Kerr <sam.kerr@finex.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state

Hi Sam / Marissa —

Quick technical notes from runtime perspective: 

- Tokens/sec vs QPS: with mixed prompt lengths, we model at token throughput (tokens/sec) because long-tail calls blow up GPU occupancy. For your numbers, conservative peak ~1,500 tokens/sec maps to ~2 x A100-class instances w/ optimized kernel paths; optimized steady-state (with batching & caching) ~300–400 tokens/sec per instance.
- Concurrency and streaming: streaming increases latency sensitivity; we recommend provisioning for p95/p99 tail with lower batch depth (so streaming sessions don't wait behind large batches). For your 40–60 concurrent streaming sessions, a configuration with 8–12 concurrent model workers and low-latency networking gave best results in our benchmarks.
- KV cache reuse: if many sessions share long prefixes (e.g., company prompt + user history), effective tokens/sec reduces by ~20–40% due to cache hits — that's significant for cost. Please provide an example prefix so we can estimate hit rate.
- Backpressure & graceful degradation: we can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant for bursts (maintain availability while controlling cost) and set per-customer token rate limits.

I can join the perf test and help interpret logs (tokens/sec, latency histograms, batch depth, kernel utilization).

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Samuel Kerr <sam.kerr@finex.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@finex.io>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: tokens/sec, peak vs steady-state

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what we needed. Next steps on our side: 

- I'll export and share a small CSV with request length distribution + an example prefix by EOD Monday.
- Please propose two 30–60 minute slots for a perf test the week of Mar 2; we prefer early morning PST.
- We'll also send a short doc with business-critical flows (to prioritize SLOs per flow).

If Redwood can share a short write-up of the two instance sizing scenarios (conservative peak mapping to instance count + recommended fallback policy), we'll include that in our procurement deck.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — speak Monday.

Sam
Samuel Kerr
Lead Product Manager, Finex
sam.kerr@finex.io
